speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I invite Members to seek clarifications if need be.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I will also make some broader comments on how we should handle such incidents as a society.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) takes a serious view of any act of bullying or violence.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: MOE monitors these cases that are reported to or are identified by our schools, whether the incidents happen in or outside schools, online or offline.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: While cases of physical bullying are relatively stable and manageable, other associated issues have arisen, especially online, to compound our concerns.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: First, the virality of social media postings has heightened sensitivities and increased social media vigilante actions.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: These can normalise the extremes and hinder rehabilitative actions.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Second, the unhelpful involvement of even a minority of adults can complicate the situation and compound the challenges faced in guiding our students.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is no higher than the national average of bullying cases in secondary schools.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This resulted in one student striking the other on the head with a plastic water bottle, giving rise to a cut on that student’s head.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The form teacher intervened immediately on witnessing the scene and separated the students.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The injured student received first aid for the cut on his head, while the school leaders called for an ambulance to convey him to hospital.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Based on MOE’s investigations so far, the school had acted appropriately to support the student’s well-being.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The school had ensured that he received medical care in a timely manner.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: During his medical leave, the school maintained communication with his parents, provided learning support for the child and monitored his well-being.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The school has also been assisting the Police in their ongoing investigations of the case.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The student who struck the other student has been suspended, is counselled and will face further disciplinary actions when he returns to school.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The school will also facilitate the restoration of relationships between the two students when they are both back in school.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The objective of these educative and restorative efforts is to help students learn and grow through these experiences.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Without the full facts, let us not speculate or jump in to complicate matters further.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Regarding the incident involving a former student of Admiralty Secondary School who fell from height in 2023, MOE is deeply saddened by this loss and our condolences are with her family and loved ones.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: When it happens, our school leaders seek to extend help to affected students and families and work closely with families in managing their grief.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: When our schools manage these situations, MOE maintains strict confidentiality and does not disclose details of the incidents or the child’s family circumstances to the public out of respect for the family’s privacy and in view of the sensitive nature of these matters.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: However, this often leaves our school leaders and teachers vulnerable to misunderstanding, leading to online attacks and abuse of our teachers and staff while they continue to exercise restraint and sensitivity to the families.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Given that this particular student’s case has now been made known to the public, I would like to assure Members of the House that the school had gone above and beyond in supporting this student when she was experiencing emotional challenges.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: When the school was informed that the student was going through some friendship issues, the school took action to guide the affected students to resolve their differences and to reconcile.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: A dedicated team comprising experienced school staff and school counsellor extended counselling to her and facilitated restorative conversations amongst the schoolmates.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Even after this incident, when the student experienced other challenges, the school continued to provide support and intervention over several months.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Throughout this process, the school staff maintained communication with the student’s family, reaching out to work with and support them.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The one-sided allegations lobbed at Admiralty Secondary do not reflect the full picture.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They do not do justice to the efforts that the school had made to help the student and her family in her time of need.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The outcome was not something anyone wished to see happen.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But the intent and efforts of the school to help the child and the family, seeking to partner the family, should not be doubted.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: When such incidents happen, some of us, including adults, may react reflexively or emotionally.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The court of public opinion, often with an incomplete view, then reacts and complicates an already difficult situation.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: MOE is particularly concerned when adults take to social media or turn up in our schools to threaten our staff, demanding action on behalf of their children, or even threatening the other children.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We will do all that is necessary, including taking firm action in accordance with MOE’s Engagement Charter and our laws to safeguard the well-being of our staff and students while we work to counsel and discipline the students involved.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: While these incidents are few, they incur disproportionate amount of time and bandwidth to manage and must not be allowed to grow.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: While a small number of parents may think the schools have not done enough in their eyes to address their grievances, we can all be confident that our teachers have the best interests of our students at heart and will deal with all of them, take care of them impartially, and not just a few or selected ones.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is useful to remember that it is one thing for children to fight and quarrel.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is quite another for adults to jump in, take sides, aggravate the quarrel and detract us from guiding our children towards reconciliation and rehabilitation.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In the recent incidents, school leaders were flamed online, the school was unfairly represented and the steadfast efforts of our educators to support all affected students were left unacknowledged and unappreciated.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I understand that many of us care deeply about the well-being of our students.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Compassion forms the foundation of a strong, nurturing society that we all strive to build.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: One, what we hear and see online may not be what it is, especially when we only choose to hear and see what we want.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Two, he who shouts the loudest and fastest, may not be the most innocent nor most accurate.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Three, swinging the sword of vigilantism in the dark, online and in real life, always hurts the innocent ones that one may claim to protect.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Four, broadcasting the extremes will normalise the extremes and encourage even more extreme behaviours.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Five, when we amplify one-sided perspectives, we should have a care if we are not being used to further the agenda of specific individuals.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Providing partisan support to feuding parties would only fuel the fire and embolden the feuding parties to be even more strident, making reconciliation more difficult.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Punishment alone, without due care to rehabilitate, is not in line with the long-term developmental interests of our children.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: An eye for an eye, makes us all blind and robs us of our future and humanity.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Eight, we are our children’s most important role models.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If we act like bullies, offline or online, they will too.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Threatening, doxxing and being disrespectful to other children and teachers are not actions that make our children better.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is also not how we demonstrate to our children that we care for them and protect them.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Nine, subverting the schools’ authority, by appealing to external “higher” authorities or seeking to use the media to attack and cast aspersions on our schools and teachers, will make us all losers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Ultimately, our children will no longer respect authority.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Such actions also take up the precious time and bandwidth of our teachers, at the expense of other children and parents who deserve more.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Ten, when we, as adults and parents, shield our children who have done wrong from punishment, we are teaching them the wrong lessons – that perhaps they do not have to take responsibility for their actions, that perhaps someone else is always at fault, or that they will always be bailed out.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, Mr Speaker, Sir, let us work together.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Let us not let the unrepresentative actions of a small minority colour the perception and behaviour of our children, our parents, our teachers and our schools.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As parents and members of the public, let us work with our teachers to be positive role models, carefully considering how we should respond in ways that are helpful and kind.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: By sharing and responding to information thoughtfully and respectfully, we contribute to building a wiser and more compassionate society.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I agree with the Minister that rehabilitation is very important and it is very difficult to maintain a fine balance between punishment and rehabilitation.
